Ted Smith and George Checkley found the start a very fast one indeed and early on they seemed well back, but towards the finish they were gaining many places and claiming their rightful positions.
George Checkley did not have one of his happiest races, yet stuck to his task and, walking a tremendously fast last lap, finished in eighth position.
The remainder of our team walked extremely well and with Ray Hall, Ray Middleton, George Checkley and John Knifton we easily won the scratch team race.
The race was won, at his first attempt, by Ray Middleton, who was ably supported by George Checkley and Bernard Eglinton. The continued improvement of Johnny Morris was particularly noted.

We are pleased to learn that George Checkley is recovering from his illness, and hopes to start training again. Congratulations to Terry Clark on his recent wedding to Janet.

Barking to Southend walk, George Checkley finished third covering the 33 miles in 5:33:27.

Hugh Mc Greechan was almost back to his very best form, George Beecham turned in his usual reliable Championship performance, Jim Morris did splendidly on his first effort, and George Checkley whipped in a really excellent team of eight men.

George Checkley showed that he is returning to his old form after a 2 year layoff, Cyril Yescombe improved on his seasons best times by over 2 minutes, but Dave King after travelling up from Bournemouth was unfortunately pulled early in the race.

- George Checkley finished 11th in the Middlesex "20" and his form (final time 3:10.23) suggests that he is slowly returning to fitness. In the same race Cyril Yescombe was timed at 3:36,47 in finishing 24th.
Eric Hall made a welcome return to 'civilisation' and finished a good third. Handicap honours went to George Checkley.

The club was successful in a match with the M.P.A.A. held in conjunction to the tune of 34 to 71 points. The handicap result was a resounding win for George Checkley who bamboozled the handicapper completely.

They last met in the mid-50's when Jack looked after him and his pupil George Checkley in his last walk in Club colours (was it the Birmingham Outer Circle 25 miles or the Leicester Mercury 20 miles race) and Jack well remembers his belief in 'rice pudding'.
Behind him Belgravian George Checkley was second in 1956 and 3rd the following year. The Club won the "Edward Knott" Team Shield in 1956, 57 and 58.
Our heartiest congratulations to all, particularly George Checkley (9th) who celebrated his birthday by gaining his honours badge. Bernard Eglington (13th) missed his by one position.
Paul Blagg won the Barking to Southend 33 mile walk on May 18th to become the first Belgrave man to win since George Checkley in 1954. Paul Blagg also won the British Police 3 Kms.
